issue.title: Rails 4.1 undefined method `each' for nil:NilClass

repository.name: activeadmin
repository.description: The administration framework for Ruby on Rails applications.

issue.body:
Hi. 

When I don't have any comment, index page displays correctly but when I get at least one comment I get this.

```
Showing .../app/views/active_admin/resource/index.html.arb where line #1 raised:

undefined method `each' for nil:NilClass
  insert_tag renderer_for(:index)
```

Do you have an idea if it's a bug or I missed something ?

Thank you !

body:
I think this worked by accident. If you have a string key, the table you link to, should have a string primary key. Creating the things table as follows will solve the issue:

``` ruby
  execute "CREATE TABLE things (id varchar PRIMARY KEY)"
```

You're probably justified in thinking that this was accidental behavior, since there were apparently no tests for it. Be that as it may, Active Admin has been depending on this behavior for years now so its built-in commenting system works for any model, whether it uses a string or a number as its primary key.

Despite my vested interest in seeing this fixed, I think the old behavior is a very useful feature for polymorphic associations and shouldn't be removed between 4.0 and 4.1.

We used to `to_s` to compare PK & FK. There was no test, but it is a regression.

We could check corresponding column types and only `to_s` if they don't match.

issue.title: Gemfile-free dependency specification

repository.name: bundler
repository.description: Manage your Ruby application's gem dependencies

issue.body:
It's only suggestion of a new feature. After working a couple months in open-source I've noticed that a lot of developers made a next snippet 

``` ruby
unless File.exist?('Gemfile')
  File.write('Gemfile', <<-GEMFILE)
    source 'https://rubygems.org'
    gem 'rails', github: 'rails/rails'
    gem 'sqlite3'
  GEMFILE

  system 'bundle'
end

require 'bundler'
Bundler.setup(:default)

# dependent code 
```

It will be nice if bundler siplifies this process. For example, in this way:

``` ruby
require 'bundler/inline'

gemfile do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  gem 'rails', github: 'rails/rails'
  gem 'rspec'
end

# dependent code 
```

What do you think about it?

issue.title: Fix polymorphic eager load with foreign_key as String.
issue.body:
The foreign_key could be `String` and just doing `owners_map[owner_key]`
could return `nil`. 
To fix this bug, we should `to_s` the keys if their type are different.

@seanlinsley Thanks for the test case.

cc @jeremy 

Fixes #14734.

issue.body:
The following test case shows the issue:

``` ruby
diff --git a/activerecord/test/cases/associations/eager_test.rb b/activerecord/test/cases/associations/eager_test.rb
index 991b0a8..d95cb46 100644
--- a/activerecord/test/cases/associations/eager_test.rb
+++ b/activerecord/test/cases/associations/eager_test.rb
@@ -1248,4 +1248,8 @@ class EagerAssociationTest < ActiveRecord::TestCase
       assert_equal 2, author.posts.size
     }
   end
+
+  def test_including_association_based_on_sql_condition_and_no_database_column
+    assert_equal pets(:parrot), Owner.including_last_pet.first.last_pet
+  end
 end
```

issue.title: [ActiveRecord] Eager Loading fails when using string primary key
issue.body:
Classes:

``` rb
class Project < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_many :tokens
end

class Token < ActiveRecord::Base
  belongs_to :project
end
```

PK/FK:
Project primary key (projects.id) is a `VARCHAR`
Token foreign key (tokens.project_id) is a `VARCHAR`
